title: Scaling choreography: runtime contracts and safety choreography
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Design and implement a 'scaling choreography' layer in the Dedicated autoscaler that interprets runtime contracts (throughput contracts and latency contracts), selects a target metric set, and executes scale actions as a coordinated sequence rather than discrete one-off steps. The choreography formalizes staging (probe -> warm -> commit), defines explicit safety fences (max delta, surge budget, rollback windows), and exposes runtime contract landmarks for observability and customer SLAs.

Goals:
- Provide a declarative contract that maps customer throughput/latency goals to runtime target selectors (e.g., tokens/s, requests/s, p99 latency).
- Implement a choreography engine that sequences scaling phases with tunable hold times and rollout animations to avoid oscillation and KV-cache churn.
- Add safety limits: per-tenant max-scale-per-minute, grace windows, conservative warm-up lanes, and a surge escrow ledger that decays.
- Surface contract state and decisions in Console and telemetry for postmortems.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Dedicated fleet autoscaler runtime and controller changes, console flags for configuring contracts, and telemetry instrumentation.
- Non-goals: Model-level kernel selection or per-GPU scheduling changes (handled by serving runtime teams), and global policy DSL rework (this uses an adapter to existing policy compiler).

Target metrics and selectors:
- Primary selectors: sustained tokens/s (30s-5m windows), p99 inference latency (30s window), and queue depth (instant).
- Composite targets: convert customer "throughput commit" into token/s with model-specific tokenization factors and optional cost-weighting.
- Fallback targets: when latency increases but tokens/s stable, prefer concurrency/latency-driven descent rather than simple token throttling.

Scaling algorithms (choreography phases):
1) Probe: small, bounded bump (5-10%) to validate headroom and warm critical KV shards.
2) Warm: allocate warm lanes with conservative concurrency to allow KV cache residency to stabilize (configurable time and ramp).
3) Commit: finalize allocation to meet target throughput; release surge budget as credits.
4) Steady: monitor composite metrics for drift.
5) Retreat: on violation, apply staged rollback with backoff and credit restitution.

Safety limits and heuristics:
- max_scale_delta_per_minute: default 20% of fleet capacity (tenant-configurable).
- MAX_ABSOLUTE_SCALE: ceiling set by tenant's committed reservation + burst cap.
- surge_escrow_budget: initial budget = min(10% reserved capacity, 200 tokens/sec equivalent); decays exponentially over 30min.
- rollback_window: 60s probe, 5m warm window, 15m full rollback horizon.
- kv_stability_guard: avoid deallocating nodes holding >X% of hot KV references during first 10m after commit.

Telemetry and experiment plan:
- New contract events stream (contract_evaluated, probe_started, warm_allocated, commit_applied, rollback_initiated) to eventstore and Console timeline.
- Add synthetic tenant harness to staging that drives steep load and verifies choreography phases under controlled failure injection (node termination, slow gpu).
- Metrics to monitor: scale_actions/sec, oscillation_index, kv_miss_rate post-scale, cost_delta_per_scale.

Acceptance criteria:
- Choreography engine accepts a runtime contract and produces a phase plan that can be simulated (unit tests + simulator).
- In staging, choreography reduces oscillation index by >=40% vs current baseline under bursty load.
- No customer-facing SLO regressions in 7-day canary window; rollback triggers and trace links present on Console.

Rollout plan:
1) Ship choreography engine behind feature-flag for internal tenants.
2) Run 2-week internal canary with synthetic and low-risk customers.
3) Enable gradual opt-in for customers with dedicated reservations, with a toggle in Console and API.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive commit improves cost predictability but increases KV churn; we favor conservative warm lanes to protect latency.
- Surge budgets improve availability for short bursts but increase short-term cost; default budgets are small and tenant-configurable.

Open questions / knobs to finalize:
- Default decay profile for surge_escrow_budget (exponential vs linear).
- Exact kv_stability thresholds (need measurement from serving runtime on shard heat).
- Whether to surface a high-level DSL for contracts or keep contract format JSON+guided templates.

Artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Scaling+Choreography+Design
- Autoscaler simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler-sim/tree/feature/choreography
- Draft PR for choreography controller: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controller/pull/482
